summary: A durable fix for the live immutable-event laundering class can use Git first-write blob identity rather than immediate-parent event comparison or a self-authored validation marker. For every event path ever added in the authoritative swarm-control ancestry, trusted validation should require the current path to exist and its current Git blob to equal that path's first-add blob. This detects rewrites/deletions even after one or more red descendants become the new parent. Transition recovery may allow an existing event change only when the after blob equals its first-write blob, giving a safe one-way exact restoration rule for the three already-laundered review events without permitting arbitrary mutation.
evidence: The Swarm workflow already checks out full Git history (`fetch-depth: 0`) for ownership/control validation, so first-add commit/blob identity is available from trusted repository history without relying on mutable .swarm/generated state.

Immediate-parent transition-check failed mutation commit ebc699fc416346e5a6dc6cc02f6d992b635f205f but later descendant 2074c342925c19d4e49916c5f33786c42be60dda passed because the rewritten event matched its immediate parent; a first-write blob check would reject both states until restoration.

Enumerating every event path ever added in current ancestry, rather than only currently present paths, also detects a historical event deletion after the deletion commit becomes a future parent baseline.

For recovery, accepting a changed event only when its after blob equals that path's first-write blob is a general one-way restoration exception. Authority, WorldEntity, and cart can then be restored exactly; any other rewrite remains invalid.

Product pr-ownership should perform the same first-write history check against origin/swarm-control before trusting its stateDigest marker; otherwise a marker matching a corrupted current tree can still bless altered event history.
PR #315 comment 5251035148 records the concrete algorithm and adversarial regression matrix.

metadata.recommendedCheck: current event blob == first-add blob for every event path ever added in authoritative ancestry
metadata.recommendedRestorationRule: existing event change allowed only when after blob equals first-write blob
